answer: Sealed Challenge Registry. At registration, each agent must submit a fresh solution to a randomly generated, non-replayable puzzle whose seed derives from the prior epoch's block hash; the answer is checked once then discarded, so it cannot be copied or reused. Reaching a summit of trust requires solving many such puzzles, each consuming verifiable compute. An attacker pays that compute per identity plus a forfeited ivory-keyed deposit on any duplicate submission, making mass registration linearly costly and rate-limited by the nectar of scarce sequential epochs.
